primary_sources.title: Trilinear Kloosterman fractions II: subdyadic intervals and nearly balanced convolutions
primary_sources.author: Thomas Wright
primary_sources.checked: Theorem 2.1 and its X^(-7 eta/5) subdyadic comparison
primary_sources.verdict: The theorem is not directly applicable to the unpartitioned top box because both denominator supports must be subdyadic. Partitioning both full supports and using scalar triangle loses more than the unchanged A^(1/2) branch gains; the nominal X^(-7 eta/5) comparison belongs to the other dominant branch. It also has nonzero phase and supplies no completed cross-sector cancellation.

primary_sources.title: Trilinear Kloosterman fractions I: partially fixed moduli and unbalanced convolutions
primary_sources.author: Thomas Wright
primary_sources.verdict: This is the scalar theorem used in the local R84/R105 top-box ledger; it is weaker than the physical estimate at j*theta asymp X^2.

primary_sources.title: Bilinear forms with Kloosterman sums via quadratic characters
primary_sources.verdict: The exact R105 transform produces a full Fourier support and a modular-inverse image rather than the two native short additive supports; no completed varying-modulus lift is supplied.

primary_sources.title: Exponential sums over primes
primary_sources.authors: James Maynard, Mayank Pandey, and Maksym Radziwill
primary_sources.verdict: For alpha=z/X in the principal band, B=max(1,|z|); the N/sqrt(B) term is natural size for z=O(1) and the theorem does not estimate cancellation with the continuum center. Even at |z|=X^(1/100), its squared normalized scale is X^(99/100), above X^(49/50).

primary_sources.title: On the level of distribution of Goldbach primes and its applications
primary_sources.author: Mizuki Akeno
primary_sources.verdict: An almost-all Goldbach-prime distribution theorem, with neither the every-window quantifier nor the completed R71 source.
